title: Task-based runbook adapter for interactive admin utilities
creator: Asha Patel
description: Enable a lightweight adapter that converts documented runbook steps into first-class task executions (tasklets) that support interactive admin utilities. The adapter should let on-call and SREs run common maintenance actions from the Console or CLI with built-in dry-run, RBAC checks, audit logging, and automated rollback hooks. This reduces toil, standardizes safety checks, and makes manual ops reproducible and observable.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter can import a runbook JSON spec and expose each step as an executable tasklet with metadata (inputs, outputs, timeout)
Console UI lists imported tasklets with 'Run', 'Dry Run', and 'Inspect' actions and enforces RBAC before execution
CLI subcommand (opsctl task-run) can execute a tasklet with --dry-run flag and prints a generated execution plan without side effects
Every execution emits structured telemetry and an audit record with requestor, params, and result status to the audit-log stream
Tasklets support pre-checks (quota, health), post-checks, and configurable automatic rollback steps mapped to runbook reversal instructions
End-to-end automated test that runs a safe 'simulated drain' tasklet in staging and validates telemetry and rollback triggers
implementation_notes: Keep adapter shallow: translate runbook step -> tasklet proto rather than reimplementing DSL
Leverage existing runbook dry-run execution engine (see ENG-271991) for simulation path
Use authz middleware in Console and opsctl to call the runbook-exec service; do not bypass existing RBAC checks
Expose a 'safety token' gating large-impact tasklets requiring two-person approval via the Console
Persist audit records to the existing immutable audit table; include a compact execution diff for easy triage
steps: Design runbook->tasklet mapping spec and review with SRE (due 2026-02-14)
Prototype import flow that converts Confluence runbook JSON to tasklet bundle
Implement opsctl CLI integration: opsctl task-run <tasklet-id> with --dry-run and --params
Add Console UI surface for listing and running tasklets with approval flow
Integrate telemetry and audit logging, wire to dashboards for a pilot team
Run staging pilot with two internal teams, gather safety regression metrics
Iterate on rollback semantics and finalize release notes and runbook templates
notes: 2026-02-11: Kickoff with SRE; agreed to support two approval modes (manual + safety token)
2026-02-12: PM feedback: prioritise clear failure messaging and per-step idempotency markers
2026-02-15: Demoed prototype import; found 3 commonly-misformatted runbook step types (db-migration, kv-rotate, cache-warmup)
2026-02-16: Infra asked for execution timeouts defaulting to 10 minutes with override up to 2 hours for migration tasks
2026-02-17: Security review scheduled; provided dataflow diagram and attack surface notes
Next: complete CLI tests and staging pilot, then schedule canary release to one internal team
rollback_plan: Every tasklet must declare an explicit rollback step or tag 'no-rollback'
On failed commit, run post-failure rollback steps automatically unless user disables auto-rollback
If rollback fails, escalate to on-call with pre-filled incident template and attach execution trace
qa_tests: Unit: translation of 12 canonical runbook step types to tasklet proto
Integration: opsctl --dry-run prints plan and returns exit 0 without side effects
E2E: staging pilot executes simulated drain with telemetry and triggers rollback when pre-check fails
Security: verify RBAC and audit log entries for each operation
